records.label: Negro boy
quotes: Severe congenital hypoprothrombinemia in a Negro boy.

records.label: Case of congenital hypoprothrombinemia
quotes: Study of a case of congenital hypoprothrombinemia

records.label: Large family with dysprothrombinemia
quotes: A large family has been studied, 11 of whose members have half-normal plasma concentrations of biological prothrombin activity. The pattern of inheritance is autosomal.
affected family members have been shown to possess normal quantities of immunoreactive prothrombin, whose immunologic properties seem identical with those of the normal zymogen.

records.label: Four siblings with prothrombin Barcelona

phenotypes.text: congenital abnormality of the prothrombin molecule

quotes: Congenital abnormality of the prothrombin molecule (factor II) in four siblings: prothrombin Barcelona.

records.label: Patient with prothrombin Quick
quotes: One of the first patients previously identified by Quick and his associates as having a defect in her plasma prothrombin has been shown to have about half the normal amount of prothrombin antigen but virtually no prothrombic function.

records.label: Hypoprothrombinemic patient described by Quick
quotes: An additional patient also first described by Quick was found to be truly hypoprothrombinemic--that is, to lack both functional and antigenic prothrombin.

records.label: 72-year-old male (prothrombin Houston)

phenotypes.text: discrepancy between prothrombin coagulant activity and antigen levels

quotes: A 72-yr-old male with a lifelong history of easy bruisability and posttraumatic bleeding had a prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time.
The presence of a dysprothrombin was confirmed by the discrepancy between plasma prothrombin coagulant activity and prothrombin antigen levels.

records.label: Identical twins (prothrombin Gainesville)

phenotypes.text: reduced plasma prothrombin activity (23% and 25% of normal) with 70% of normal prothrombin antigen

quotes: A pair of identical twins was evaluated for menometrorrhagia and mild post-operative bleeding. Each had a slightly prolonged partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time.
Full hemostatic evaluation was normal, except that plasma prothrombin activity was 23% and 25% of normal with a Russell's viper venom assay. Each twin had 70% of normal plasma prothrombin antigen.

records.label: French family with prothrombin Metz

phenotypes.text: abnormal prothrombin generating thrombin less sensitive to antithrombin III inactivation

records.segregation: Father heterozygous for hypoprothrombinemia, mother heterozygous for dysprothrombinemia; 3 children double heterozygotes; all genetic combinations observed
quotes: Investigation of a mild hemorrhagic tendency in a French family revealed the father to be heterozygous for hypoprothrombinemia while the mother was heterozygous for dysprothrombinemia.
Among the children the double heterozygosity encountered in 3 of them allowed us to discover an abnormal prothrombin, prothrombin Metz
records.genotype_reason: two different heterozygous variants in one gene

records.label: Propositus

phenotypes.text: prothrombin activity less than 10% with antigen about 50%
abnormal anodic immunoelectrophoretic migration of prothrombin

records.segregation: Father had ~50% prothrombin activity and antigen; mother had 45% activity but ~100% antigen
quotes: The propositus was a 5-year-old female who presented with umbilical bleeding after birth followed by easy bruising and bleeding tendency throughout her life.
Prothrombin activity was less than 10% in several one- and two-stage systems. However, the staphylocoagulase-complexed prothrombin level and immunologic methods yielded levels of about 50%.
Family studies revealed that the father had approximately 50% prothrombin activity and antigen, whereas the mother had 45% prothrombin activity but about 100% prothrombin antigen.

records.label: Propositus (prothrombin Segovia)

phenotypes.hpo_label: Bleeding with minor or no trauma

phenotypes.text: very low functional prothrombin activity (7% one-stage, 20% two-stage) with normal immunologic level

records.segregation: Consanguineous parents both had 50% reduced prothrombin levels with physiological activators or Echis carinatus venom
quotes: The propositus is a 21-yr-old man who presented simultaneously with hemartrosis of the left knee and an extensive hematoma following a minor trauma. Prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time were prolonged.

Family studies revealed consanguinity between the propositus' mother and father and both presented a 50% reduced prothrombin level when physiological activators or Echis carinatus viper venom were used.

records.label: Propositus (newborn girl, prothrombin Poissy)

phenotypes.text: very prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time
prothrombin activity about 2% in one-stage assay
prothrombin antigen 47% with abnormal migration in crossed immunoelectrophoresis

records.segregation: Father, mother and brother had both normal and abnormal prothrombin in plasma
quotes: A new congenital dysprothrombinaemia is described in a newborn baby girl who presented severe bleeding from the second day of life.
Routine coagulation tests showed very prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time with about 2% prothrombin activity in a one-stage assay.
Family study revealed the presence of both normal and abnormal prothrombin in the plasma of three family members: the father, the mother and the brother.

records.label: Proband (prothrombin Tokushima)

phenotypes.text: reduced prothrombin clotting activity (12% of normal)

quotes: A mutant prothrombin, designated prothrombin Tokushima, was purified from plasma of a proband with 12% of normal plasma clotting activity and 42% of normal prothrombin antigen.

records.label: Mexican family with prothrombin Mexico City

phenotypes.text: structurally abnormal prothrombin with more acidic isoelectric point

quotes: Prothrombin "Mexico City," an asymptomatic autosomal dominant prothrombin variant.
A functionally normal but structurally abnormal prothrombin variant was found in a Mexican family.

records.label: Prothrombin Magdeburg family

phenotypes.text: reduced ratio of factor II clotting activity to factor II concentration (about 0.5)
abnormal prothrombins with higher molecular weight and lower isoelectric point

records.segregation: Seven affected members over three generations; affected persons heterozygotes
quotes: Seven members of one family over three generations were found to have a characteristic reduction to about 0.5 of the ratio between factor II clotting activity and factor II concentration
This is an autosomal hereditary dysprothrombinemia, the affected persons being heterozygotes.
Five of the seven persons had a slightly increased bleeding tendency which manifested itself especially in more marked or prolonged posttraumatic and postoperative bleedings.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Proband (compound heterozygote, prothrombin Tokushima/hypoprothrombinemia)

variants.as_reported: single nucleotide substitution responsible for dysprothrombinemia of prothrombin Tokushima
single base insertion of thymine (T) at position 4177; frameshift from codon 114, premature termination codon (TGA) at codon 174

quotes: A single nucleotide substitution responsible for dysprothrombinemia of prothrombin Tokushima was detected, as were three polymorphisms.
Sequencing of PCR-amplified genomic DNA revealed a single base insertion of thymine (T) at position 4177.
The inheritance of the hypoprothrombinemia gene from the father to the proband was proved by PCR-SSCP with endonuclease digestion and mutated primer-mediated PCR-RFLP.

records.label: Proband with prothrombin Tokushima

variants.as_reported: substitution of thymine (T) for cytosine (C) at position 9,490, changing arginine (Arg) to tryptophan (Trp) at position 418

records.segregation: Mutant gene inherited from the proband's mother
quotes: The gene for prothrombin Tokushima was shown to be inherited from the mother of the proband.

Sequencing analysis using PCR-amplified genomic DNA clarified a substitution of thymine (T) for cytosine (C) at position 9,490, changing arginine (Arg) to tryptophan (Trp) at position 418 of the polypeptide chain.

records.label: Proband (Prothrombin Himi)

phenotypes.text: dysfunctional prothrombin with reduced fibrinogen clotting activity

variants.as_reported: T to C transition at position 8751, Met-337-->Thr (Thrombin Himi I)
G to A transition at 8904, Arg-388-->His (Thrombin Himi II)

records.segregation: Met337Thr inherited from father, Arg388His from mother; one sister also inherited both alleles
quotes: A congenitally dysfunctional form of prothrombin, Prothrombin Himi, shows reduced fibrinogen clotting activity, although it retains full hydrolytic activity toward synthetic substrates.

One is a T to C transition at position 8751, resulting in the substitution of threonine for methionine at codon 337 (Thrombin Himi I). The other is a G to A transition at 8904, resulting in the substitution of histidine for arginine at codon 388 (Thrombin Himi II).
By sequencing analysis of her parents, it was determined that Thrombin Himi I was inherited from the father and Thrombin Himi II from the mother.

records.label: Propositus

phenotypes.text: hypoprothrombinemia (Factor II activity 2%, Factor II antigen 5%)

variants.as_reported: A-->G substitution in exon 3, Tyr44 (TAC) by Cys (TGC)

records.segregation: Both parents heterozygous; complete cosegregation of the mutation with prothrombin deficiency
quotes: A patient with a severe bleeding tendency and hypoprothrombinemia (Factor II activity 2%, Factor II antigen 5%) was screened for the presence of alterations in his prothrombin gene.
revealed that the patient was homozygous for an A-->G substitution in exon 3. This substitution predicts the replacement of Tyr44 (TAC) by Cys (TGC) in the prothrombin molecule.
Both parents were found to be heterozygous for the same mutation.

records.label: Five homozygous sibs of the propositus
records.segregation: Complete cosegregation; only homozygous sibs clinically affected
quotes: Only the five homozygous brothers and sisters of the propositus were clinically affected (severe hemorrhages including epistaxis, soft tissue, muscle and joint bleedings in all, and severe hemorrhages in the two women).
Further family studies revealed complete cosegregation of the mutation with the prothrombin deficiency.

records.label: Prothrombin Denver proband
quotes: The original patient with prothrombin Denver had a severe haemophilia-like bleeding disorder treated with weekly prophylactic factor replacement.
Analysis of factor II activity and antigen in the patient showed a factor II activity of 5 units/dl and factor II antigen of 21 units/dl.
This moderately severe dysprothrombinaemia was found to be associated with compound heterozygosity for two different Glu-->Lys point mutations, at amino acid positions 300 and 309.

records.label: 13 patients with prothrombin deficiency
quotes: Of 11 patients with hypoprothrombinemia, ten are homozygous for five mutations and one patient is a compound heterozygote. The two patients with dysprothrombinemia are homozygous for two mutations.

Eight of nine mutations are missense ones associated with single amino acid substitutions in the propeptide (Arg-1Gln, Arg-2Trp), the kringle-1 (Asp118Try) and kringle-2 (Arg220Cys) domains and the catalytic serine protease domain (Gly330Ser, Ser354Arg. Arg382His and Arg538Cys).
The ninth mutation is an in-frame deletion of 3 bp that results in the omission of one amino acid (del Lys 301/302).

notes.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) distinguished 2 main phenotypes of prothrombin deficiency: hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency), with concomitantly low activity and antigen levels, and dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency), with normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein. Hypoprothrombinemia associated with dysprothrombinemia was also described in some compound heterozygous cases.
quotes: Two main phenotypes can be distinguished: (1) hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency), characterized by concomitantly low levels of activity and antigen; and (2) dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency), characterized by the normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein.
In some cases, hypoprothrombinemia associated with dysprothrombinemia was also described in compound heterozygous defects.

notes.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) stated that prothrombin deficiency is among the rarest inherited coagulation disorders, with a prevalence of approximately 1 in 2,000,000.
quotes: Prothrombin deficiency is among the rarest inherited coagulation disorders, with a prevalence of approximately 1:2,000,000.

notes.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) noted that no living patient with undetectable plasma prothrombin had been reported.
quotes: No living patient with undetectable plasma prothrombin has been reported to date.

notes.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) reviewed 40 different mutations identified in prothrombin deficiency. Many surround the catalytic site, another hotspot is in anion binding exosite I (fibrinogen recognition site), and mutations were also found in the Na(+)-binding loop and the thrombin light A chain. Most hypoprothrombinemia-associated mutations are missense, but nonsense mutations and a single-nucleotide deletion were also reported.
quotes: Forty different mutations have been identified and characterized in prothrombin deficiency. Many of them surround the catalytic site, whereas another "hot spot" is localized in the recognition domain called anion binding exosite I, also called fibrinogen recognition site.
Recently, mutations were identified also in the Na (+)-binding loop and in the light A-chain of thrombin.
Most hypoprothrombinemia-associated mutations are missense, but there are also nonsense mutations leading to stop codons and one single nucleotide deletion.

notes.statement: In a systematic review of 46 articles, Segal et al. (2009) found that heterozygosity for prothrombin G20210A did not predict recurrent venous thromboembolism in probands compared with individuals without the variant (OR 1.45; 95% CI 0.96-2.2). They also found the evidence insufficient on whether homozygosity predicts recurrence and on the risk of VTE in family members.
quotes: Heterozygosity for prothrombin G20210A is not predictive of recurrent VTE in probands compared with individuals without prothrombin G20210A (OR, 1.45; 95% CI, 0.96-2.2).
Evidence is insufficient regarding the predictive value of prothrombin G20210A homozygosity for recurrent VTE and the risk of VTE in family members of individuals with prothrombin G20210A.

notes.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) described prothrombin (factor II) deficiency as a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder occurring in approximately 1 in 1 to 2 million people. Both hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia have been described.
quotes: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder that occurs in approximately 1 in 1-2 million people.
Both hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia have been described.

notes.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) noted that bleeding in prothrombin deficiency is mostly mucosal or follows surgery or trauma. Joint bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage have also been reported.
quotes: Clinical manifestations are predominantly mucosal or surgical- or trauma-associated bleeding, but joint bleeding and intracranial haemorrhages have been reported.

notes.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) noted that low prothrombin activity typically prolongs both the activated partial thromboplastin time and the prothrombin time. The hemostatic level of prothrombin is thought to be 20 to 40%, and its half-life is approximately 3 days.
quotes: Low prothrombin activity typically prolongs both the activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time.
The haemostatic level of prothrombin is thought to be between 20 and 40%, and the half-life is approximately 3 days.

notes.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) stated that no purified prothrombin products are available for replacement therapy. Fresh frozen plasma and prothrombin complex concentrates both contain prothrombin and may be used for treatment.
quotes: No purified prothrombin products are available for replacement therapy. Both fresh frozen plasma and prothrombin complex concentrates contain prothrombin and may be used for treatment.

notes.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) noted that more than 40 mutations in prothrombin are known.
quotes: There are more than 40 known mutations in prothrombin.

notes.statement: VAN CREVELD (1954) reported on congenital idiopathic hypoprothrombinemia.
quotes: Congenital idiopathic hypoprothrombinemia.

notes.statement: Akhavan et al. (2000) described prothrombin deficiency as an autosomal recessive disorder associated with a moderately severe bleeding tendency.
quotes: Prothrombin deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder associated with a moderately severe bleeding tendency.

notes.statement: Using crystal structures of alpha-thrombin and prothrombin fragments 1 and 2, Akhavan et al. (2000) inferred that hypoprothrombinemia mutations affect propeptide cleavage from the Gla domain, stability of the kringle-1 and -2 domains, or the close association of the A and B chains of the serine protease domain, whereas dysprothrombinemia mutations directly affect catalytic function through their location at the active site crevice or exosite 1.
quotes: The hypoprothrombinemia mutations were inferred to affect either the cleavage of the propeptide from the Gla domain, the stability of the kringle-1 and -2 domains, or the close association of the A and B chains of the serine protease domain.
The dysprothrombinemia mutations were inferred to directly affect catalytic function through their location at the active site crevice or exosite 1 within the serine protease domain.

notes.statement: Lefkowitz et al. (2000) found that assays of plasma from the prothrombin Denver proband suggested that the functional defect lay in the activation of the zymogen to the enzyme.
quotes: Assays of plasma from the prothrombin Denver proband suggested that the functional defect was in the activation of zymogen to enzyme.

notes.statement: Lefkowitz et al. (2000) described dysprothrombinemia as a rare congenital cause of bleeding. They noted that fewer than 25 families with a functional prothrombin (factor II) defect had been reported.
quotes: Dysprothrombinaemia is a rare, congenital cause of bleeding. Fewer than 25 families who express a functional prothrombin (factor II) defect have been reported.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) noted that prothrombin deficiency was first described in 1947 by Quick et al., and that the first prothrombin abnormality was reported in 1969 by Shapiro et al.
quotes: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency was first described in 1947 by Quick et al., although the first prothrombin abnormality was reported in 1969 by Shapiro et al.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) stated that prothrombin deficiency or abnormality can be diagnosed with a combination of clotting, chromogenic and immunologic assays. In true deficiency, all these assays decrease in parallel whatever the activating agent. Discrepancies among the clotting assays, particularly with viper venoms, should raise suspicion of dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: The diagnosis of prothrombin deficiency or abnormality can be made using a combination of clotting, chromogenic and immunological assays. In cases of true deficiency, a parallel decrease in all these assays is observed, regardless of the activating agent.
If discrepancies among the clotting assays are noted, particularly using viper venoms, a dysprothrombinemia should be suspected.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) reported that in true deficiency, activity levels are usually less than 10% of normal in homozygotes and 40 to 60% in heterozygotes. In congenital dysprothrombinemias, factor II levels are more variable, usually 1 to 50% of normal. In these cases antigen levels are normal, near normal or slightly decreased, but always higher than the clotting activity.
quotes: Usually, activity levels less than 10% of normal are found in homozygotes, and between 40 and 60% in heterozygotes.

Usually the levels of factor II vary between 1 and 50% of normal. Antigen levels in congenital dysprothrombinemias will be normal, near normal or slightly decreased but always higher than the clotting counterpart.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) noted that patients with dysprothrombinemia may be homozygotes, heterozygotes, or compound heterozygotes. Compound heterozygotes may carry a heterozygous abnormality together with a heterozygous true deficiency, or two distinct abnormalities. The authors added that cases with a parallel decrease in prothrombin activity and antigen should not be considered examples of hypoprothrombinemia.
quotes: Factor II levels in congenital dysprothrombinemias are more variable since one may encounter homozygotes, heterozygotes and compound heterozygotes between a heterozygous abnormality and heterozygous 'true' deficiency or between two distinct abnormalities.
Cases with a parallel decrease in prothrombin activity and antigen should not be considered as examples of hypoprothrombinemia.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) reported that bleeding may be severe in homozygous true deficiency, where hemarthroses and intracranial bleeding have been described. Bleeding is more variable in dysprothrombinemias, and heterozygotes are usually asymptomatic. Prognosis generally follows the prothrombin activity level.
quotes: Bleeding manifestations may be severe in homozygous 'true' deficiency and may be more variable in dysprothrombinemias. Heterozygotes are usually asymptomatic.
In homozygous true deficiency, hemarthroses and intracranial bleeding have been described.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) noted that the prothrombin gene is located on chromosome 11 and has 10 exons. Molecular studies had found several point mutations in some of the dysprothrombinemias.
quotes: The gene involved in the synthesis of prothrombin is located in chromosome 11. It is composed of 10 exons and 8 introns. Molecular biology studies have discovered several point mutations in some of the dysprothrombinemias.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) stated that substitution therapy uses prothrombin complex concentrates or plasma. Because injected prothrombin has a long half-life of about 70 hours, hemostatically effective levels (about 50% of normal) are achieved without difficulty.
quotes: Substitution therapy is based on the administration of prothrombin complex concentrates or of plasma. The long half-life of prothrombin injected, about 70 h, allows the achievement of hemostatically effective levels (about 50% of normal) without difficulty.

notes.statement: Poort et al. (1994) found that in a family with a homozygous prothrombin Tyr44Cys mutation, only homozygous individuals were clinically affected, and concluded that the bleeding tendency appeared to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: Only the five homozygous brothers and sisters of the propositus were clinically affected
The bleeding tendency therefore seems to inherit as an autosomal recessive trait.

notes.statement: Weinger et al. (1980) found by crossed immunoelectrofocusing that the prothrombin antigen of a patient with prothrombin Houston was more basic than normal, although crossed immunoelectrophoresis was similar to normal and the prothrombin was completely adsorbed onto and eluted from barium sulfate.
quotes: Crossed immunoelectrofocusing, a procedure combining isoelectric focusing in disc gels with electroimmunoassay in the second dimension, demonstrated that the patient's prothrombin antigen was more basic than normal.
His plasma prothrombin was capable of being completely absorbed onto and then eluted from barium sulfate.

notes.statement: Weinger et al. (1980) showed that prothrombin Houston was cleaved by Echis carinatus venom, yet the activated eluate clotted purified fibrinogen more slowly than normal, suggesting that the coagulopathy results from generation of a dysfunctional thrombin.
quotes: SDS-slab gel electrophoresis revealed that the prothrombin present in the patient's eluate was cleaved by Echis carinatus venom.
These studies suggest that the coagulopathy of prothrombin Houston results from the generation of a dysfunctional thrombin.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (1981) gathered prothrombin kinetic data in twins with prothrombin Gainesville before and during hysterectomy. Infused prothrombin (Konyne) had a volume of distribution of about 1.5 times the plasma volume and a half-life of 34 hours.
quotes: Prothrombin kinetic data were obtained before and during hysterectomy. In these twins, infused prothrombin (Konyne) was found to have a volume of distribution of approximately one and one-half times the plasma volume and a half-life of 34 hours.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (1981) reviewed the dysprothrombins reported before their study and stated that prothrombin Gainesville was the twelfth such disorder reported.
quotes: The previously reported dysprothrombins are briefly reviewed. Prothrombin Gainesville is the twelfth such disorder reported.

notes.statement: Josso et al. (1982) found that the abnormal prothrombin Metz generated an abnormal thrombin that was less sensitive to inactivation by antithrombin III than normal thrombin.
quotes: prothrombin Metz, which generates an abnormal thrombin less sensitive to inactivation by antithrombin III than normal thrombin.

notes.statement: Board et al. (1982) used a new electrophoretic technique to find three allelic variants at the prothrombin structural locus (FII). One allele, FII4, reached polymorphic frequencies in some Pacific Island populations.
quotes: This technique has revealed three allelic variants at the prothrombin structural locus (FII). One of these alleles (FII4) reaches polymorphic frequencies in some Pacific Island populations.

notes.statement: Board et al. (1982) studied the activated products of three variant prothrombins. In each case the structural variation was on a profragment, not on the enzymatically active thrombin molecule.
quotes: Investigation of the activated products of the three variant prothrombins has demonstrated that, in each case, the structural variation is located on a profragment and not on the enzymically active thrombin molecule.

notes.statement: Rabiet et al. (1984) purified thrombin Metz after activating the variant prothrombin with factor Xa. By physicochemical criteria it was identical to normal thrombin. However, it had less than 4% of normal fibrinogen clotting activity, abnormal Km and Kcat on S2238, and less than 5% of normal effectiveness in inducing platelet aggregation.
quotes: By physicochemical criteria, thrombin Metz is identical to normal thrombin.
Thrombin Metz exhibits less than 4% of fibrinogen clotting activity. Both Km and Kcat, determined on S2238, are abnormal.
Thrombin Metz is less than 5% as effective as normal thrombin in inducing platelet aggregation.

notes.statement: Rabiet et al. (1984) found that thrombin Metz released both fibrinopeptides A and B more slowly than normal, with B more affected, which slowed fibrin polymerization. Its interaction with antithrombin III was slower than normal, but not in the presence of heparin. Thrombin Metz also bound less tightly to heparin-Sepharose.
quotes: A decreased release rate for both fibrinopeptides, more marked for fibrinopeptide B, results in a slow fibrin polymerization, as followed by absorbance at 450 nm.

Interaction with antithrombin III is slower than normal when followed by SDS gel electrophoresis and inhibition of the amidolytic activity of thrombin on S2238. This abnormality is not observed in the presence of heparin.
However, thrombin Metz binds less tightly to a heparin-Sepharose column, and the direct inhibition of heparin on its activity on S2238 is weaker.

notes.statement: Rabiet et al. (1984) predicted that the defect in thrombin Metz affects the catalytic site or its vicinity. They proposed that, jointly or as a consequence, it also affects the region where thrombin interacts with antithrombin III and heparin. Supporting this, fluorescence enhancement of the DAPA probe on binding to thrombin Metz was only 34% of that seen with normal thrombin.
quotes: Titration with the high-affinity competitive inhibitor of thrombin, DAPA, shows that fluorescence enhancement of the probe is only 34% in binding to thrombin Metz when compared to that observed in binding to normal thrombin.

From these results, we can predict that the defect in thrombin Metz affects the catalytic site or its vicinity and, jointly or consequently, the region of interaction of thrombin with antithrombin III and heparin.

notes.statement: Rubio et al. (1983) found that the abnormal prothrombin (prothrombin Habana) migrated more anodically in single and bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis, and its migration did not change with the addition of calcium.
quotes: The migration of the abnormal prothrombin was more anodic in single and bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis system and did not change by the addition of calcium.

notes.statement: On the basis of family studies, Rubio et al. (1983) suggested that the propositus was a compound of heterozygosity for an abnormal prothrombin (inherited from the mother, who had 45% activity but normal antigen) and heterozygosity for true prothrombin deficiency (from the father, who had about 50% activity and antigen).
quotes: We suggest that the propositus is heterozygous for an abnormal prothrombin and heterozygous for true prothrombin deficiency.
Family studies revealed that the father had approximately 50% prothrombin activity and antigen, whereas the mother had 45% prothrombin activity but about 100% prothrombin antigen.

notes.statement: Lanchantin et al. (1968) determined the amino acid composition of human plasma prothrombin.
quotes: Amino acid composition of human plasma prothrombin.

notes.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) isolated prothrombin from the plasma of an affected person and obtained normal amounts of protein but only half the normal prothrombin activity. When activated by intrinsic or extrinsic systems, concentrated sodium citrate, or trypsin, it gave half or less of the expected thrombin clotting and esterase activity.
quotes: Prothrombin isolation from the plasma of one such individual gave normal yields of protein but half-normal amounts of prothrombin activity.
gives rise to half, or less, of the thrombin clotting and esterase activities expected from a comparable normal prothrombin preparation.

notes.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) found that serum from an affected person contained a normal 'pro piece' plus an additional activation product of intermediate electrophoretic mobility. They suggested that affected individuals are heterozygotes in whom half the prothrombin molecules are structurally abnormal. These molecules change during activation but cannot release active thrombin.
quotes: Immunoelectrophoresis of the serum reveals a normal nonthrombin "pro piece," and an additional activation product with an electrophoretic mobility intermediate between that of prothrombin and of "pro piece."

These results suggest that affected individuals are heterozygotes in whom half the prothrombin molecules synthesized are structurally abnormal, since they undergo some alterations during activation, but are incapable of releasing the active enzyme, thrombin.

notes.statement: Josso et al. (1971) used the name prothrombin Barcelona for a congenital abnormality of the prothrombin (factor II) molecule that they found in 4 sibs.
quotes: Congenital abnormality of the prothrombin molecule (factor II) in four siblings: prothrombin Barcelona.

notes.statement: Girolami et al. (1974) described prothrombin Padua, a 'new' form of congenital dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: Prothrombin padua: a "new" congenital dysprothrombinemia.

notes.statement: Valls-de-Ruiz et al. (1987) found that prothrombin Mexico City had a more acidic isoelectric point (4.01) than normal prothrombin (4.29) but a normal molecular weight. Factor Xa and Echis carinatus venom cleaved it abnormally, although both produced functionally normal thrombin. Its calcium binding and overall antigenic structure were normal.
quotes: Immunoisoelectricfocusing studies revealed that this variant has a more acidic isoelectric point (4.01) than normal prothrombin (4.29), but it proved to have a normal molecular weight

Two-dimensional immunoelectrophoresis studies showed an abnormal cleavage of the prothrombin molecule by factor Xa and Echis carinatus venom as well, despite the fact that both yield functionally normal thrombin molecules.
the ability of the molecule to bind calcium ions as well as its overall antigenic structure were investigated and found to be normal.

notes.statement: Valls-de-Ruiz et al. (1987) suggested that the abnormality was a simple (substitution or translocation) mutation in the fragment 2 region. Because the variant differed from previously described ones, they proposed the name prothrombin 'Mexico City'.
quotes: These results taken together suggest a simple (substitution or translocation) mutation at the fragment 2 level.
Since this prothrombin variant is different from others described previously, the name "Mexico City" is proposed to identify it.

notes.statement: Inomoto et al. (1987) found that thrombin Tokushima, made by factor Xa activation, had a normal molecular weight but less than 22% of normal clotting activity. Its kcat/Km for a synthetic substrate was less than one-tenth of normal, although active site titration showed no difference from normal thrombin.
quotes: The molecular weight of thrombin Tokushima estimated by SDS-PAGE was identical to that of "thrombin."
Thrombin Tokushima exhibited less than 22% of normal clotting activity, and the value of kcat/Km (mumol/L-1 second-1) was less than one tenth of that of "thrombin"
However, active site titration using p-nitrophenyl-p'-guanidinobenzoate failed to detect any difference between the two.

notes.statement: Inomoto et al. (1987) found that thrombin Tokushima was 2.5% as effective as normal thrombin at inducing platelet aggregation and 33% as effective at forming a complex with antithrombin III. They concluded that the molecular defect lies in the thrombin portion of the molecule and that the binding sites for various substrates appear to be greatly impaired.
quotes: Thrombin Tokushima was 2.5% as effective as "thrombin" in inducing platelet aggregation.
Based on the residual thrombin activity, it was 33% as effective as "thrombin" in forming a complex with antithrombin III.
These results indicate that the molecular defect resides in the thrombin portion of prothrombin Tokushima and that the binding sites for various substrates appear to be greatly impaired.

notes.statement: Dumont et al. (1987) found that in the propositus with prothrombin Poissy, staphylocoagulase and Echis carinatus venom prothrombin assays gave 35% and 25%, respectively, while prothrombin antigen was 47%. Thrombin generation in a system free from natural inhibitors showed that the abnormal prothrombin was slowly and incompletely activated, and the propositus was thought to be homozygous for a 'lazy' dysprothrombin.
quotes: Staphylocoagulase and Echis carinatus venom prothrombin assays were respectively 35% and 25%.
Thrombin generation in a system free from natural inhibitors showed that the abnormal prothrombin was slowly and incompletely activated.
The propositus is thought to be homozygous for a 'lazy' dysprothrombin.

notes.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) found that prothrombin Segovia had very low activity with physiological activators (7% one-stage, 20% two-stage), Russell's viper venom-cephalin (23%), Notechis scutatus scutatus venom (15%) and Echis carinatus venom (17%). In contrast, the level was borderline to normal with Taipan venom (64%) and normal by staphylocoagulase and immunologic methods.
quotes: Prothrombin activity was very low when measured by biological assay using physiological activators (7% by one-stage method and 20% by two-stage method) or a Russel's viper venom-cephalin mixture (23%), Notechis scutatus scutatus venom (15%) and Echis carinatus venom (17%)
in contrast, the level was found to be borderline to normal using Taipan viper venom (64%) and normal by both staphylocoagulase and immunologic methods.

notes.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) observed a line of identity between normal prothrombin and prothrombin Segovia on immunodiffusion. The abnormal prothrombin migrated less anodically, and adding calcium did not change its migration. On bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis, the patient's serum showed 3 bands, compared with 2 bands in normal serum.
quotes: A line of identity between normal and abnormal prothrombin was observed on immunodiffusion. The migration of the abnormal prothrombin was less anodic and was not changed by the addition of calcium.
The patient's serum showed 3 bands in the bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis system, whereas normal serum showed only 2 bands.

notes.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) proposed the term prothrombin Segovia for this new congenital prothrombin abnormality.
quotes: The term prothrombin Segovia is proposed to define this new prothrombin abnormality.

notes.statement: Lutze et al. (1989) found that the reduced ratio of factor II clotting activity to factor II concentration in prothrombin Magdeburg was not seen when prothrombin was measured after activation with staphylocoagulase. SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis showed, in addition to normal prothrombin, two abnormal prothrombins with higher molecular weights and lower isoelectric points.
quotes: which was not seen when measuring prothrombin after activation with staphylocoagulase
In addition to the "normal" prothrombin, two abnormal prothrombins, with higher molecular weights and lower isoelectric points, were found by SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.

notes.statement: Morishita et al. (1992) used PCR-SSCP analysis of exons 8 through 14 of the prothrombin gene (encoding the thrombin moiety) in a family with Prothrombin Himi and identified two variant conformers in exon 10; one allele from the father and one from the mother were both inherited by the proband and one of her sisters.
quotes: identified two variant conformers in exon 10 specific to this family. One variant allele detected in the father was inherited by the proband and one of her sisters, and the other detected in the mother was also inherited by them.

notes.statement: Morishita et al. (1992) noted that Prothrombin Himi showed reduced fibrinogen clotting activity while retaining full hydrolytic activity toward synthetic substrates.
quotes: A congenitally dysfunctional form of prothrombin, Prothrombin Himi, shows reduced fibrinogen clotting activity, although it retains full hydrolytic activity toward synthetic substrates.

notes.statement: In prothrombin Tokushima, Iwahana et al. (1992) found a C-to-T change at nucleotide 9490 of the prothrombin gene. The change replaced arginine with tryptophan at position 418 (Arg418Trp). They considered this mutation the likely molecular basis for three reasons: Southern blot analysis showed no distinct changes, the variant protein had the same molecular weight as the abnormal gene product, and no other amino acid abnormalities were found in the proteolytic peptide fragments.
quotes: This point mutation is assumed to be the molecular basis of prothrombin Tokushima, firstly, because of the absence of distinct changes in Southern blot analysis of the proband's DNA
This is the first report of gene analysis of dysprothrombinemia.

notes.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) detected the abnormal prothrombin gene in two ways: by its altered migration on PCR-SSCP and by the loss of an MspI site on PCR-RFLP. They concluded that both methods were useful for detecting the abnormal gene and for directly diagnosing carrier status in dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: The abnormal gene was detected by altered migration by PCR-SSCP and by the loss of an MspI site by PCR-RFLP.
It is concluded that PCR-SSCP and PCR-RFLP were useful for detecting the abnormal gene and for directly diagnosing the carrier status of dysprothrombinemia.

notes.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) found that a 1-bp insertion of T at position 4177 in exon 6 of the prothrombin gene caused a frameshift altering the amino acid sequence from codon 114 and creating a premature stop codon at codon 174 in exon 7. Because exon 7 encodes the kringle 2 domain preceding the thrombin sequence, they concluded that this frameshift leads to a null prothrombin phenotype.
quotes: The resulting frameshift mutation caused both an altered amino acid sequence from codon 114 and a premature termination codon (i.e., TGA) at codon 174 in exon 7.
Because exon 7 encodes the kringle 2 domain preceding the thrombin sequence, this frameshift leads to the null prothrombin phenotype.

notes.statement: Owen et al. (1978) proposed that the dysfunctional prothrombin in a patient originally described by Quick, with about half-normal prothrombin antigen but virtually no prothrombin function, be designated prothrombin Quick.
quotes: We propose that this dysprothrombin be designated prothrombin Quick.

notes.statement: Owen et al. (1978) noted that 10 families with true hypoprothrombinemia and 6 families with dysprothrombinemia (a functionally abnormal prothrombin) had been reported, along with 8 further families with an unclassified prothrombin abnormality.
quotes: Only 10 families with significant reductions of this plasma protein (hypoprothrombinemia) have been observed. Even fewer, six families, have been found to have a functionally abnormal prothrombin (dysprothrombinemia) in their blood.
An as yet undefined prothrombin abnormally has been recognized in eight other families.

notes.statement: Rabiet et al. (1979) studied how the abnormal prothrombin Barcelona is activated and found evidence for active high molecular weight intermediates.
quotes: Activation of prothrombin Barcelona. Evidence for active high molecular weight intermediates.
